title: Unroll a loop body
starter:
let unroll (n : int) (body : string list) : string list =
  []

samples.expect: float v = a[0]; | b[0] = v; | float v = a[1]; | b[1] = v; | float v = a[2]; | b[2] = v;
samples.label: unroll 3 ["float v = a[@];"; "b[@] = v;"]

hints: You need every counter value `0` to `n - 1` on the outside and every line of `body` on the inside. `List.init n f` builds one item per counter value.
`String.concat (string_of_int r) (String.split_on_char '@' line)` gives one line with every `@` replaced by the number `r`.
`List.concat (List.init n (fun r -> List.map (fun line -> String.concat (string_of_int r) (String.split_on_char '@' line)) body))`

answer.explain: The outer loop walks the counter values in order and the inner loop walks the body in order, so the copies come out in the same order the loop would have run them. That is all unrolling is: the loop is gone, the counter is a number in each copy, and every statement still runs in its old place. Your renderer does the same thing with real nodes in place of strings.
